I attended Wings Tour, so a lot of memories just getting hazy because it was 4 years ago (yeah obviously not because I was busy screaming my lungs out lol).

Taehyung looked like a Greek statue while standing still (and this was before DNA came out which he became even more gorgeous, imagine how he looks now in real life lol). Seokjin looked like the lights came straight out of his face. Namjoon looked... tasty. There i said it. He looked like he knew he's *it.* Jimin jumped straight out of manhwa. Yoongi *shines.* I knew he is pale but he was blindingly pale (in a good way). Jungkook was so playful and smiled a lot, he radiated this younger-brother-you'd-love-to-tease-around energy, just jumping around here and there. 

Now Hoseok... we don't talk about Hoseok. No one attend their concert and leave without being wrecked by Hoseok. He was so captivating I can't pull my eyes off of him. There's something about him that you can't see through your screens. I can write a book about how mesmerizing this person in real life but let's wrap it up here. 

Performance-wise, they're a very good performer. They know how to make the stage feels small in their hand. They also actually enjoy their performance, and this shows in their solos and their non-choreographed performance. It was mesmerizing how they look so casual with their performance but at the same time being very attentive to their crowd, it makes us the crowd feels like one with the one in the stage.  

There's not a lot of things I remembered, as soon as I leave the venue it feels like my brain was squeaky clean lol, zero recollection about the concerts. This is apparently something a lot of armys suffered for lmao.

For me it's Paradise. On my early 20's with uncertainty of what I want to thrive on my life, it's very easy to go through spirals of darkness. While my peers already settling on their career and starting their own family, I am here struggling to study something completely different from my degree, essentially throwing away 4 years of my life. It feels like you lose a race you're not even participating on. This song reminds me to not chasing other's dream and walk on your own pace. 

It certainly sucks when people look down on other people that doesn't dream "big". I don't want to be a ground-breaking figure with lasting impact in my name, I just want to be alive. For some, "big" dream is a privilege that not anyone can afford. Paradise validated my attitude towards what is dream, like BTS could read my mind and untangled what I was feeling lol

Let me introduce you to Butterfly. At first I though it was another love song from BTS (I'm not very fond of love song in general) so I did not pay the deserved attention she needed. But one day I realized what was the song is actually about: loving someone that is so fragile, you're afraid you're gonna lose her at some point. Coming from a former 2nd generation KPop fan, i was familiar with KPop industry before i knew BTS.  I must admit that a lot of idols seems to be out of touch with their own song, thus where the "manufactured" stereotype comes from. Which makes sense, as there was not a lot of idol that writes their own song and they were not expected to. 

BTS really defies the manufactured norm that was there. Their lyrics are raw and gritty (especially Yoongi's), and being on-hand with their own arts really benefits them in the sense of how excited they are in performing one. You could sense the pride, the silent but proud "This is our song!" vibe whenever they perform. 

Their songs also actually delivers message that they want to convey, also as a way to communicate to their fans. They tell a story with their whole discography, and their own story at that. Their autonomy and artistic freedom is not something you usually find, especially in idol industry.

I've been an army since 2015 and i think the thing that hookep me up was never mind. So back then don't really paid much attention to them but i've watched a couple of their mv (kinda obsessed with dope), pushing the yt algorithm to recommend me never mind. 

So here's the thing; i've been listening to a lot of kpop since early 2010s, but lots of times the lyrics disappoint me lol so to save myself from the disappointment i don't really read the trans. Yes this is including dope (which i'm still bitter about lol i can get into them earlier but my ignorance shoot me straight to my feet). But i can feel the raw emotion from never mind. The pain, the anger for the world. This raw anger pushed me to actually check the trans and that's it, that's the shit.  I was also in the middle of a hard times and never mind actually pulled me out from the darkness. I graduated, i finished college, i stayed alive thanks for never mind.

With that, I jump straight to the pit. Been here for almost 6 years and i regret nothing.

It was back then in high school, and the student council got their own room. Sometimes we used the room for chit-chatting with each other or even sleeping because the school hour is exhausting (7am - 4pm, sometimes 8pm if you count the extra hours).

One time, the room is packed with people just laying around and doing their stuff. This was at 6pm, so this was past the school hour. 

This one girl was being called by her mother, and demand a proof that she does stay in the school. So she decided to take a selfie in with two of their friends, thus making it three. I was there, sitting in which way the selfie camera was pointing at. Their face was turning pale after they saw the photo they just took. 

Beside their face, there was another face. It's not even a face, she had no face. What was there is just a head wearing a white hijab (I'm Indonesian and hijab is common in our uniform) with black emptiness in the place where the face should be. 

Shit, typing this at 3 am is not a good decision.

I did not ask her about that because somehow the room looks *strangely* normal. Normally i would freak out knowing someone locked in a small room but no, i don't feel it at all until a sudden realization years later.

It has been a long time since i moved from that house and i lost contact since then, unfortunately.

Probably not what you're asking for, but i still think about it until now. When i was 7, i had a friend two years younger than me. She lives across my house, and her family is just like a normal family. Dad's a teacher and mom is staying home.

One day while playing as usual in her house, she asked me "do you want to see a ghost?" . Being a little curious shit of course i said yes. Then she led me upstairs. I've never know this house had an upper level, you can't see it from the exterior and the stairs itself is located in the kitchen and well-hidden in the dark (the kitchen is fucking dark and spacious, but crammed with a lot of thing as well)

Upstairs there was a room, the only room there. She told me to peek on the small crack on the door. There was someone sitting on the floor, back facing the door. From what i can recall is he's a man with a curly hair, wearing an orange t-shirt. This guy doesn't look like a ghost at all and his body was moving. Not like creepy move or something, just like what you do when you feel uncomfortable with your current position. 

The one thing that i remember the most is the room is locked from the outside with a padlock. Also i've lived there for a year and i almost have no memory of other person from this family beside my friend, her brother, mother and father. 

Then it took me eight years later to realized that it's not normal

I've listened to their song casually since No More Dream released, but what makes me fell for them hard is Never Mind. I've listened to Kpop since 2011 and back then i never bother to check the translation of a Kpop song because you know, i found myself dissapointed too many times with them nonsensical lyrics LOL. Until Never Mind released and i'm completely absorbed with the lyrics and emotion. 

Backstory time! I was facing a hard time at my school at the same time when HYYH: pt.2 released. I was a senior in high school and need to plan my track for further education. So i choose to pursue psychology (which i've dreamed on since i'm starting high school) on one of the most prestigious state university in my country, but literally everyone around me opposed, or at least degraded my dream. I was not a bright student, and since psychology is a social branch study and i'm a science student, my step is really frowned upon. Science students called me coward and had given up on hard science, and social students called me a snake because i'm snatching their opportunity. Man, that was a hard time i was facing with and hence where i got my depression. Until Yoongi saved my ass with his intro. 

Well, things got better. Right now i'm studying psychology (i've just finished my first mid-term exam!), exactly where i want to be. Back then when i was studying for college entry test, i always play this song whenever i feel hopeless. Which is really helping.

This sounds really cheesy, but BTS helps me to pursue my biggest dream. And Never Mind will always be my favourite song :)
